Klykoliai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Klykoliai, Lithuania

Not demolished. Klykoliai's Jewish community, established in the second half of the 18th century, reached an extraordinary 93 percent of the village's population by 1897, trading across the nearby Latvian border with the cities of Liepāja and Riga. WWI devastated the community — the village itself was largely destroyed, residents were deported to the Russian interior, and returning families in 1918 found their homes expropriated by Latvian soldiers and their study house turned into a stable. A 1930s economic downturn, driven partly by organized Lithuanian opposition to Jewish businesses, drove many remaining families to emigrate, chiefly to South Africa — so that by the German invasion of summer 1941, only about 30 Jews remained in Klykoliai; all were transported to the district town of Mažeikiai and shot there on August 8, 1941. This cemetery, established shortly after the community itself, was despoiled by Latvian soldiers during WWI, but Soviet authorities did not demolish it afterward, though only 87 gravestones remained by the time of its 1992 heritage registration.
